name: Radiology
stance: Exploit data volume while improving safety

workforce.label: active physicians
workforce.definition: AAMC Radiology and Diagnostic Radiology grouping
workforce.source_label: AAMC 2022 Physician Specialty Data Report (2021 data)

need.label: U.S. patients receiving CT
need.scope_note: This is CT utilization, not disease prevalence or all radiology utilization.
need.source_label: Projected Lifetime Cancer Risks From Current CT Imaging

funding.scope_note: Biomedical imaging and bioengineering proxy; radiology research is distributed across NCI, NHLBI, NINDS, industry, and other funders.

digital_leverage.basis: High-volume digital images, mature DICOM infrastructure, established workflow systems, measurable turnaround and quality outcomes, and strong AI compatibility.

strategy.labor: Treat AI as workflow augmentation: protocoling, worklist prioritization, quality assurance, comparison retrieval, follow-up tracking, and communication—not autonomous replacement.
strategy.applications: Prioritize appropriateness, dose optimization, incidental-follow-up closure, multimodal decision support, and integration into PACS, RIS, and EHR workflows.
strategy.group: Radiology offers fast technical demonstrations, but projects should begin with deployment ownership, validation data, liability boundaries, and measurable workflow outcomes.
